encoding_choice.chosen: a line-class grammar expressed in JSON
encoding_choice.why: Every rule §14.2 makes decidable is a statement about a LINE — its class, its token shapes, and whether its class is admitted on the surface at all. A JSON Schema describes a data structure; the artifact these emitters produce is text, and the thing being constrained is the text. Expressing line classes directly means an emitter validates what it is about to print rather than a model of it, which is the distinction §14.2's own AC3 rests on.
encoding_choice.declined: JSON Schema — checkable by tooling already present in this repository (checks/check-terrain-composition.sh validates survey records against survey-schema.json), but it would require modelling rendered Markdown and terminal text as a document tree first, and that model would itself be an unchecked restatement of the format.
encoding_choice.recorded_here_because: SPEC.md §14.1 names this file and its duties and deliberately does not decide the encoding (story 1.52 SQ1). A choice made in implementation and left unwritten is one the next editor re-derives.

LessonDisplayID.means: a member's owner-facing display id, assigned once in the survey record (§14.3)
LessonDisplayID.producer: terrain/terrain.mjs cmdSurvey — minted ONCE per candidate in the survey record (§14.3), resolved at render time by displayIdOf(); story 1.53, kogaki#345
LessonDisplayID.absence_is_abnormal: A member whose survey record predates §14.3 carries no display_id. The surfaces render NO_DISPLAY_ID and state the abnormality; they NEVER substitute the slug, because the slug is what §14.3 removes and a silent fallback would undo the decision while looking like robustness. So an owner surface may carry the NO_DISPLAY_ID token in a LessonDisplayID position, and a refusal built to admit only ^L[0-9]+$ there would reject exactly the legacy record the abnormality exists to make visible.

GroupID.means: a Group's owner-facing display id, assigned once per composed screen in co-tag sort order (§6.1)
GroupID.producer: terrain/terrain.mjs cmdCotags — minted over the composed group list; kogaki#317 (story 1.56)
GroupID.carries_the_hierarchy: THE LEVEL IS IN THE TOKEN. This is the whole point of the mint: `G1` is a Group and `G1-1` is one of its SubGroups, so a line that WRAPS still says which it is. Indentation could not do that — a wrapped continuation starts at column 0 and the hierarchy vanishes exactly where the claim text is longest, which is the 2026-08-09 hands-on finding this replaces.

SubGroupID.means: a SubGroup's display id, prefixed by its parent GroupID (§6.2)
SubGroupID.parent_is_readable_from_the_id: `G1-2` names its parent without a lookup, which is what lets a SubGroup line stand alone after a wrap.

LessonCount.means: a count of Lessons, family-named per §9

Cite.shape: a served-surface citation string, rendered inside backticks
Cite.means: provenance — the address a served rendering was quoted at
Cite.status_under_14_3: Recorded here, DECIDED on kogaki#345 (story 1.53 SQ2, owner, 2026-08-11) — that issue is the authority on what was decided and this line is a pointer to it, per precedence_is_per_axis above. What it records: a served CITE is an ADDRESS rather than an element name, so §14.3 does not remove it; the PER-MEMBER `*Served line:*` row was nonetheless removed on kogaki#318's 'two name-shaped rows' ground, and the member → served-line map moved to the report's end, the siting §12 line 805 and the WA baseline (wa#1115/#1116) already named. A prior draft of this entry wrote the ruling as though this file had made it.

SubstratePin.shape: a substrate pin string, rendered inside backticks

JudgePin.means: model_id/effort_tier, or the typed literal `none` (§12.1 uniform arity)

SuggestionID.means: a provenance-neighborhood suggestion's owner-facing display id, minted over the neighborhood's own ordered output (§14.6, filled by owner selection on kogaki#300)
SuggestionID.producer: terrain/terrain.mjs NEIGHBOR_ID (:2828), minted over the sorted output at :2915
SuggestionID.disjoint_from_LessonDisplayID: DECLARED DISJOINT from ^L[0-9]+$ (§14.6). §14.3 assigns a display_id ONCE, in the survey record; a suggestion is by construction NOT in that record, so nothing there assigns it one. The two spaces coexist and no owner surface renders both for one element. A taken suggestion is assigned an L<n> by §14.3's existing assignor on the way in, and its N<n> does not follow it.
SuggestionID.absence_is_abnormal: There is no legacy case: the space is minted per pull over that pull's own output, so every suggestion in a rendered section carries one. A row in a SuggestionID position carrying anything else is a defect, not an abnormality to disclose — which is what distinguishes this token from LessonDisplayID, whose NO_DISPLAY_ID form exists for records that predate §14.3.

refusal_text_boundary.fact: No text raised through fail() (terrain/terrain.mjs:45-48) is a line of ANY owner surface this artifact grammars. fail() writes to stderr and exits.
refusal_text_boundary.scope: global — it holds for every surface here, covered or uncovered, and each surface restates it rather than inheriting it silently
refusal_text_boundary.stated_by_mechanism_not_enumeration: The boundary names the FUNCTION, not a list of messages. A list goes stale on the next fail() added and leaves message N+1 uncovered by default — the shape §14.1 and §9 both chose against.
refusal_text_boundary.reopen_trigger: the first owner-facing refusal text written to stdout, or into the report file, rather than raised through fail() — that one is on a surface and owes a line class

cotag_screen.non_member_fallback: REFUSE — a line whose class is not in line_classes is not rendered and the emitter refuses to print (§14.2). The fallback is refuse and never admit, because an enumerated prohibition's non-member fallback is admit and that is the shape §9 chose against.

line_classes.form: <tag> — the second navigation step. Grouped by co-tag; sort: <COTAG_SORT>.

line_classes.the_name_stays_and_here_is_why: Through v5 `<GroupID>` RENDERED AS the co-tag name, because no id space existed — the heading was `testing × architecture — 2 Lessons: …`. v6 mints a real id, and the name stays BESIDE it rather than being replaced by it: kogaki#317 rules the change 'presentation only … content is untouched', and the co-tag name is content that was already on the screen. A heading reading `G1 — 2 Lessons: L2, L1` would leave the owner unable to tell what G1 is about, on the surface whose whole job is showing which co-tag groups exist. Order is id, then meaning, then counts and members: the id leads because it is the carrier, and the member ids sit last at a predictable position because they are what gets copied.

line_classes.form: pinned to <n> member(s) — a subset selection RECOMPOSES and re-offers it as a gate event (SPEC.md §7)

line_classes.marker_is_what_makes_this_class_decidabl: The `> ` prefix is not decoration. Through v2 this class was `      <composer prose>` and the six-space indent was the only thing distinguishing it; v3's flush-left change removed the indent and the class silently began matching EVERY line, which took `line_class_allowlist` inert on this surface. The marker restores the distinction without restoring the layout — it carries no level, so it does not re-introduce the defect kogaki#317 fixed. Owner decision 2026-08-11 on kogaki#317, chosen over declaring the rule inapplicable here (which full_report already has to do) and over dropping the class, which would have been a content decision wearing a format fix's clothes since §6 admits machine-composed connective prose.

line_classes.form_note: The SubGroup form changed from `(N Lessons: …)` in parentheses to the same `— N Lessons: …` dash form the Group heading uses. Parentheses were carrying part of the level distinction; with the level now in the SubGroupID, two different punctuations for one shape is a difference that means nothing.

Declared as its two literal openings rather than as `<leaf reason>`, and this is the SECOND class the flush-left change caught out. `judgeSubgroup` emits exactly two shapes — `leaf: …` and `NOT a leaf: …` (terrain/terrain.mjs) — so the bare placeholder was never describing the class, it was describing nothing; through v2 the ten-space indent hid that by constraining it anyway. Same lesson as `group_prose`'s marker one entry up: a layout convention was doing a discriminator's job, and removing it exposed which classes had no description of their own. This one needed no owner decision because the RENDERED TEXT does not change — the grammar is only saying what the emitter already emits.

line_classes.form: judged by <model_id> / <effort_tier> (§6.2 — a judged surface with no judge pin is the drift-undetectable shape)
ABNORMAL: <n> of <m> group(s) on this screen carry no composed GroupClaim. …

<n> of <m> group(s) render flat because their only named SubGroup was not tighter than the parent — the split bought nothing, so it does not discharge the subdivision obligation (SPEC.md §6.2 v7, kogaki#316). …
line_classes.note: §6.2 v7 / kogaki#316 decision 3. The group renders flat and is fully conformant, so this is a DISCLOSURE and not an abnormality — but a judgment ran, produced a split and had it suppressed, and a flat group is otherwise indistinguishable from one nobody judged. Aggregate rather than per-group: a per-group line is precisely what decision 3 removes.

line_classes.form: ABNORMAL: <n> of <m> member(s) on this surface carry no display_id. … Re-run `terrain survey` to regenerate the record (§12.2 v11).
line_classes.note: Emitted at whatever indent its surface uses, so the class is matched on the ABNORMAL: prefix and its text rather than on leading whitespace. Declared because §14.3's absence case reaches the owner surface: a refusal that admitted only ^L[0-9]+$ in a LessonDisplayID position would reject exactly the legacy record this line exists to make visible.

line_classes.form: Compose them from the bounded input — compose-input --survey <F> --tag <T> — …
Cover: <n> of <m> member Lessons appear in at least one co-tag group — counted AFTER composition, over placements. Selected tag: <strandFigure>; <denominator>.
Select a group (still narrowing nothing): cotags --survey <F> --tag <T> --group "<co-tag>"

line_classes.note: The emitters separate blocks with empty lines — a trailing \n on the header (:661), the post-judge-pin blank (:725), and the \n-prefixed subgroup and cover lines. A grammar that admitted no blank line would, under REFUSE, reject every screen the emitter produces.

not_on_this_surface.see: refusal_text_boundary — the fact is global; this entry is its application to this surface
not_on_this_surface.why: fail() writes to STDERR and exits. This surface grammars the screen cmdCotags prints on stdout, so a refusal text is never a line of it. A first draft admitted COTAG_COVER_INCOMPLETE (terrain/terrain.mjs:742) and COTAG_COVER_INVENTED (:745) as line classes; both were describing text the grammar never sees, and the same draft omitted the other fail() texts on the identical path — nine of them by count at this pin. Story 1.54 would have had to pick a reading, and the artifact stated both.
not_on_this_surface.stated_by_mechanism_not_enumeration: The boundary is named as `raised through fail()` rather than as a list of messages, deliberately. An enumeration here goes stale on the next fail() added and leaves message N+1 uncovered by default — the shape §14.1 and §9 both chose against. A construction-level statement covers every message the function can carry.
not_on_this_surface.reopen_trigger: the first owner-facing refusal text written to STDOUT rather than raised through fail(), which would put it on this surface and owe it a line class

cotag_screen.indentation_is_not_a_carrier: v3, kogaki#317. NO LINE CLASS ON THIS SURFACE ENCODES LEADING WHITESPACE, and that is a contract rather than a formatting preference. Indentation was the sole carrier of subordination through v2, and the 2026-08-09 hands-on round found it unreadable for the reason it cannot fix: claim lines are long prose, they wrap at the terminal edge, and a wrapped continuation begins at column 0 — so the hierarchy disappears exactly where the text is longest. The level now rides tokens.GroupID and tokens.SubGroupID, which survive wrapping because they are content. A future edit re-introducing leading spaces to signal level is re-introducing the defect.
cotag_screen.line_class_allowlist_went_inert_here_in_: RESOLVED in the same v3, and kept as a record rather than deleted. The flush-left change removed the six-space indent that was `group_prose`'s only constraint, so the class began admitting every line and `decidable_rules.expressible.line_class_allowlist` — LIVE on this surface through v2 — had no unadmitted line left to find. It was found by the suite going red on the spec diff alone, not by review of the change, and the alternative preview shown at the deciding gate described the new appearance without naming this cost. The repair is `group_prose`'s `> ` marker above (owner decision 2026-08-11). The general shape is worth keeping: a layout convention is often ALSO a discriminator some rule leans on, and removing it changes the appearance on purpose while disarming the rule by accident — the rule keeps running and stops finding anything, which reads as a clean result. full_report's own inertness (reader_notes) is the same class arriving by a different route and is NOT repaired by this.

Three pin-bearing Gloss rows per member is what made `pin_once_per_file` pass while the pin appeared six times in a two-member report: the registered rule counts occurrences of the `substrate_pin` LINE CLASS, so it reads 1 and is silent about pins embedded in other classes.

line_classes.note: ONCE per file, AGGREGATED over the entered set (v5, kogaki#314). The stated cost: a per-section count is not shown. Per-section Counted was declined with per-section Served lines, below.

§12 (line 805, line 2366) requires the report to carry the member → served-line map, and the WA baseline sites it AT THE REPORT'S END. Until story 1.53 the renderer satisfied §12 with a per-member `*Served line:*` row instead; kogaki#318 called that the second name-shaped row and the owner removed it. The duty did not go away with the row — it moved here. v5, kogaki#314: ONCE per file, MERGED across sections and DEDUPED — a member entered under both `G5` and `G5-1` appears once. A repeated map is the class kogaki#315 named unjustified, and the dedupe is what keeps the merge honest rather than merely shorter.

Declared as its two rendered lines rather than as prose, per the defect preamble and judged_empty_notice both carried: a class declared as a description matches no rendered line, and under REFUSE that rejects every conformant file.
A member with no display_id or no cite is NAMED here with its abnormal token rather than omitted — a map that silently skips its unmappable rows is the shape §2.1 forbids.
line_classes.pin_is_not_repeated_here: v3, kogaki#315. The cite renders BARE — `file:line`, no `@<pin>` — because the substrate pin is stated ONCE, in the identity block (§12; #315's own phrasing: 'pin once in the identity and a bare file:line map, sited once'). The v2 form repeated the pin per row, which is the same clause violated in a new place: story 1.53 removed the per-member `*Served line:*` row and re-sited the map here, carrying the pin with it. Same count, different siting — recorded because a relocation reads as a fix and is not one.

line_classes.note: v6, kogaki#472, read off terrain/terrain.mjs:3306.

full_report.retired_in_v6: `h2_subgroups` (`## SubGroups`) and `h2_members` (`## Members`) are RETIRED (kogaki#314). The v7 renderer emits neither: `### <SubGroupID>` goes straight under its section heading, and the flat and judged-empty paths push members with no intervening heading. They are removed rather than kept as dead entries because §14.1 makes this file authoritative over the RENDERED form, so a class nothing produces is a claim about artifacts that do not exist — the shape `not_expressible` spent its life avoiding. uncovered_surfaces.note: SPEC-terrain §14.1 defines an OWNER SURFACE as any text this runtime prints or writes for the owner to read, and enumerates six. This grammar covers two. decidable_rules.note: SPEC-terrain §14.2's enumeration. Each is decidable on the rendered text alone, which is what makes the emit-time refusal possible. A rule that is not mechanically decidable does not enter this artifact and stays prose.

This rule counts lines of class `substrate_pin` and nothing else, so it cannot see a pin embedded in a Gloss cite or a map row. expressible.licensed_by: kogaki#316 decision 2, owner 2026-08-09; enumerated at SPEC.md §14.2 ("catch-all <= 30%")
expressible.re_bound_in_v4_because_it_measured_the_w: THIS RULE EXISTED SINCE v1 AND CAPPED A DIFFERENT QUANTITY. Story 1.52 read §14.2's "catch-all <= 30%" and bound it to `(no second served tag)` — the CO-TAG group, for Lessons carrying the selected tag and no other — over the Cover line's corpus denominator. kogaki#316's decision 2 is about `(fits no composed SubGroup)`, the SUBGROUP remainder, over the parent group's own member count. Different numerator, different denominator, same name and same number. The issue's own specimens are all the second kind — 11 of 17, 20 of 28, 29 of 35 — and nothing in the tree measured it, so decision 2 read as shipped and was not. THE CO-TAG BOUND IS REMOVED RATHER THAN RENAMED (owner decision 2026-08-11): no owner decision ever asked for it, a tagless group over 30% is a fact about the CORPUS rather than a composition defect, and refusing a screen over it would punish the substrate for its own tag distribution. It was also a number in code that nobody ratified, which is the shape §8's standing rule is pointed at.
expressible.surfaces_is_cotag_screen_only_and_that_i: The share needs a per-SubGroup count and a parent count. `cotag_screen`'s `subgroup_heading` and `group_heading_subdivided` both carry `<LessonCount>`, so it is decidable there. `full_report`'s `h3_subgroup` is `### <SubGroupID> — <SubGroup name>` and carries NO count, so the rule is NOT decidable on that surface and does not claim it. Stated rather than listing both — the sibling entry `group_subgroup_id_grammar` had to be narrowed for exactly this reason in v3, and a rule naming a surface it cannot decide is the 'reads as coverage' shape.

expressible.declared_without_a_predicate_at_first: PR #354 round 1 finding 1: this entry moved out of `not_expressible` and no predicate was written, so it was declared and could never fire — which is the exact condition the entry was in `not_expressible` to avoid, since a rule with no members 'reads as coverage'. It is carried on cotag_screen only. full_report's allowlist is inert — three body classes are bare placeholders — so `# Full Report — testing × architecture` is admitted by a body class and nothing refuses it; that is precisely how round 1 finding 2's divergence survived review of the sitting that created it. reader_notes.ac2_surface_mismatch: Story 1.52 AC2 asks that `the grammar's cotag_screen tag-row entry` match SPEC.md §9's allowlist. The co-tag screen renders NO tag rows: §9's allowlist governs SCREEN 1's tag rows, produced by tagRow() at terrain/terrain.mjs:407 and printed by the survey/view path — which §14.1 lists as `cmdView`, an UNCOVERED surface. The allowlist is therefore transcribed against cmdView above, where it actually binds, rather than attached to a surface that has no such line class. Transcribing it onto `cotag_screen` would have satisfied the AC's letter by reinterpreting the rule, which is the one thing AC2 forbids. Reported on kogaki#344.
reader_notes.completeness_of_the_line_classes: The classes were read off the emitters, and three reviews have found the same defect class three times: a declared form that no rendered line matches, which under REFUSE and §14.1's precedence rejects every artifact the emitter produces. Round 1 of kogaki#349 found no blank-line class; round 2 found judged_empty_notice declared as one line where two are pushed, and found the two COTAG_COVER classes describing stderr text this surface never sees; round 1 of kogaki#350 found preamble carrying the same one-line-for-four defect — in the entry the previous fix had cited as its own precedent. `blank` is a class on both surfaces; the refusal classes are removed and replaced by refusal_text_boundary; preamble and judged_empty_notice now declare their literal lines. The general hazard stands and is stated rather than claimed away: this enumeration is only as complete as the read that produced it, and a class discovered missing is found by story 1.54's refusal rejecting a valid render. Story 1.55's golden fixture is what converts that from a live-run discovery into a CI one.
reader_notes.what_this_artifact_is_not:
Not a second carrier beside the golden fixture (§14.5) -- the fixture never wins against this file; precedence is one-way. Not an enforcement mechanism -- story 1.54 installs the emit-time refusal that reads this. 

CORRECTED AT v6 (kogaki#472). This note previously read 'Not a description of §13's provenance neighborhood, which is unimplemented and whose display-id question is a named deferred slot'. Both halves were false by 2026-08-12 and neither was corrected when it became so: §13 was implemented at kogaki#302/#303, and the display-id slot was FILLED by owner selection on kogaki#300 (§14.6, the N<n> space). As of v6 this file DOES describe the neighborhood -- as a section of full_report, not as a surface of its own -- so the sentence is removed rather than merely re-dated. Kept as a correction rather than deleted, because a note asserting a thing is undescribed is exactly the shape that survives the thing being described.
reader_notes.form_notation_tolerances: Three tolerances the story-1.54 predicate applies when reading a `form`, declared here because a reader comparing the grammar to the code would otherwise find them only in terrain/format-guard.mjs. (1) A LEADING `\n` denotes the blank line before the class, not two characters of it — the emitters separate blocks with `\n`-prefixed strings and this file transcribes them as written; the blank itself is the `blank` class. (2) A form containing `…` is matched as a PREFIX, because the ellipsis abbreviates the rest of a long fixed line; anchoring the tail would make the abbreviation STRICTER than the text it abbreviates, which is the `preamble` and `judged_empty_notice` defect in another costume. (3) TRAILING whitespace is admitted, because a Markdown hard break is two trailing spaces and this notation cannot write them; the identity block emits three such lines. None of the three admits a token, class or line this file does not already admit.
reader_notes.line_class_allowlist_is_inert_on_full_re:
Found while firing the refusal in its refusing direction (story 1.54, kogaki#346). `group_claim_body`, `subgroup_claim_body` and `member_gloss_body` each have a bare placeholder as their whole form, so each admits ANY line; on full_report there is therefore no line that can be unadmitted, and `decidable_rules.expressible.line_class_allowlist` is inert there. It is live on cotag_screen, whose classes are constrained. Recorded rather than repaired: constraining a claim body is a decision about this artifact, owed its own licensing issue, and story 1.54 narrowing it from the emitter side would be the shape `narrowing_withdrawn` already names twice. 

WIDENED, NOT REPAIRED, AT v6 (kogaki#472). The neighborhood section's sixteen classes land on this surface, and fourteen of them are CONSTRAINED — the suggestion row, the bound line, the per-family figures. They inherit the inertness anyway, and the mechanism is `class_matching_is_by_specificity`: a MALFORMED neighborhood row fails its own specific class, falls through to `group_claim_body`, and is admitted. So the exemption is a property of the SURFACE, caused by three classes and reaching every class on it, including classes added long after the three were written. 

STATED AT THE WIDENING RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER, because that is what the served position asks of exactly this act: 'When a rule carries an exception justified by one member's genuine constraint and the rule's scope is later widened, the exception travels with it onto members that never had the constraint -- and because an exception exists precisely in order to skip a check, its wrongful inheritance emits no error, no warning and no failing test, so re-derive every exception at every widening and withdraw it unless the new member can state the original justification in its own terms.' (consulted: product-lab@8906f20752e27d1935c62f24c8ba41ea1d55dba0 LESSONS.md:64, an-inherited-exemption-signals-nothing). The neighborhood classes CANNOT state the original justification in their own terms -- they are not claim bodies and nothing about them needs a free-form form -- so by that line the exemption is owed a withdrawal, and this note records that it was NOT withdrawn here. What blocks the withdrawal is unchanged and is the note's own first paragraph: constraining the three body classes is a decision about this artifact and belongs on its own issue, and kogaki#472's licence names the amendment, not that decision. 

What v6 buys anyway, so the coverage claim is not read as empty: the classes are DECLARED, so `no_element_names` and `pin_once_per_file` reach the section, the golden fixture (SPEC §14.5) is owed a specimen that exercises its forms, on kogaki#473, and a renderer edit that changes a form now diverges from a written contract instead of from nothing at all. What is missing is only the emit-time REFUSAL of a line that matches no class. 

See `deferred_slot_full_report_allowlist` below for the fork, which is named and not decided.
reader_notes.class_matching_is_by_specificity: Classes are matched most-specific-first, specificity being the count of literal non-space characters a form pins outside its placeholders — not declaration order. `group_prose` (`      <composer prose>`) admits every six-space-indented line including every `subgroup_heading`, so first-match-wins classified subgroup headings as prose and `subgroup_members_sum_to_parent` summed zero and refused a conformant screen. Order would have fixed that case and left the next one silent: a class added in the wrong place shadows another and nothing says so.

precedence_is_per_axis: THIS FILE WINS ON THE RENDERED FORM AND ON NOTHING ELSE. §14.1 makes it authoritative over what an owner surface's text may look like — the BUILT axis. It is NOT authoritative over what was DECIDED: where an entry records an owner ruling, the ruling's home is the issue named beside it and this file carries a POINTER, not the verdict. Written down because the two halves are answered by different systems and one rule for both hands this file the last word on facts it cannot observe (consulted: product-lab@4cc496b39be1d7641aaaaf678668fb64eda35f17 gloss/lessons/knowledge-architecture.md:227 — 'Say which system decides which half'). Added after PR #352 round 1 recorded consultation-map entry 3 UNCOVERED for the second consecutive PR on this chain; the consult that entry prescribes is what produced this paragraph, and the first thing it found was that the entries below had been written in the wrong voice.

deferred_slot_full_report_allowlist.what_is_owed: A decision on whether full_report's three bare-placeholder body classes (`group_claim_body`, `subgroup_claim_body`, `member_gloss_body`) are constrained, so that `line_class_allowlist` becomes live on this surface -- or whether a SECTIONED allowlist is admitted instead, refusing only lines under a heading whose section declares a closed class set. The second shape would make the rule live for the neighborhood section without touching the claim bodies at all.
deferred_slot_full_report_allowlist.why_it_is_a_decision_and_not_a_fix: Both shapes change what the emit-time refusal REJECTS, which is the artifact's contract with every producer and every fixture. Constraining a claim body decides what a composer may write; a sectioned allowlist introduces a second scoping axis to a file whose whole precedence argument rests on one. Neither is settled by reading the code, so it is owed on its own licensing issue with alternatives and a receipt BEFORE any predicate embeds an answer.
deferred_slot_full_report_allowlist.not_filed_here: Filing it now would be `conditional-on:` shaped -- its validity turns on which shape a future sitting takes -- and SPEC-issue-creation refuses that filing, folding it into the deciding issue's acceptance items instead. Named here so the slot is visible rather than rediscovered.
